title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation day - our favourite classroom.


The first week has been a whirlwind of challenges and delights, but reflection is needed after failing to complete 3 labs and multiple worksheets. The instructors and TAs are fantastic, and my colleagues were bright and encouraging. However, staying late and grinding slowly did not work.
This week’s game plan: 1. Rule 1: Do all worksheets and all labs ASAP. 2. Rule 2: Changes for pre-lecture readings:

Math: Ask AI to explain the textbook simply if you struggle with the textbook for 10 minutes.
R: Watch Dr. Timbers’s videos first (not the textbook or required readings).
Platforms: Reading first does not help if you don’t understand 80% of it.
Python: Read through ahead of class. Watch a YouTube video ifneed be. Haven’t figured this class out.

It feels doom-y, but it’s definitely not gloomy. Instructors and students are the highlight of each day. Onwards.

title: About

title: About
text:
Why data science
Despite the wide range of jobs, the same questions kept resurfacing: What insights can be extracted from it? How can those insights be communicated persuasively? How can systems outlast the people who build them? And how can AI and automation make work faster and more accurate, freeing up time for deeper analysis?
After more than a decade of trying to learn on her own, Joyce decided to enrolled in UBC’s Master of Data Science program. She’s interested in statistics, modelling, and the process of turning messy data into something meaningful. The learning curve is steep, but she’s enjoying the challenge and has been continually impressed by her instructors and cohort.

title: About
text:
Outside of Data
Joyce leans into her “granny hobbies” that include cooking, movies, reading, knitting, and arts and crafts, and visiting museums.
She top-rope climbs and is working toward climbing 10s with the goal of learning how to lead by the summer of 2027. Her ultimate dream is to be able to climb outdoors in different countries as she travels.
Please congratulate Joyce on recently becoming a long-distance owner of a stray cat! “Trash Kitty” was found eating scraps from the bin behind her brother’s London flat, and after only four days of whispering sweet promises of a warm bed – and four cans of tuna– the cat finally wandered into their home where he established himself as their newest and most adorable family menace.
